record.title: safeEqual leaks BOARD_TOKEN length via early return on length mismatch
record.description: Code pattern verified in source: safeEqual at features/board/worker/src/index.js lines 56-62 returns false immediately at line 58 when lengths differ, skipping the constant-time loop at lines 59-62; authed() at lines 64-69 passes the supplied key and env.BOARD_TOKEN to safeEqual, and the fetch handler at line 346 returns an identical 401 for any failed auth. In principle this is a length oracle, but only via timing: the response body/status is identical for wrong-length and wrong-value keys, no live timing measurement was attempted or provided, the signal is a sub-microsecond loop difference versus millisecond-scale Cloudflare edge/network jitter, and knowing the length alone reveals no key content and does not materially aid guessing a high-entropy secret.

trace.what: fetch handler calls authed(request, env) for /api/* and returns identical 401 on false
authed() passes supplied key and env.BOARD_TOKEN to safeEqual(key, env.BOARD_TOKEN)
safeEqual returns false immediately on a.length !== b.length, skipping the constant-time XOR loop on lines 59-62

record.conditions: No live timing measurement was attempted; the only observable difference is timing, with an identical 401 response for wrong-length and wrong-value keys.
record.remediation: Proposed remediation is correct as optional hardening, not as a required vulnerability fix: hash both values (e.g. SHA-256 via crypto.subtle) and compare the fixed-length digests in constant time, or loop over max(a.length, b.length) accumulating diff without an early return and decide only after the loop. Either removes the gross length branch; note plain JS loops are still not strictly constant-time under JIT, so the hash-compare form is preferred.
record.reason: Fails the 7-Question Gate and should be rejected as a finding, demoted at most to an optional hardening note: Q1 fails — no copy-pasteable request yields any data, since the 401 is identical either way and length is only hypothetically learnable via timing; Q6 fails — impact is only 'technically possible' with no demonstrated measurement, statistical sample, or attacker-attainable outcome, and the skill directs that a single wrong gate answer kills the finding. The exploitable signal is a sub-microsecond loop skip swamped by millisecond Cloudflare edge jitter, and length alone gives no key content, so there is no tangible impact to report even as confirmed-informational.
